simple.meaning: אַחֲלַי (ʼachălay) is a Hebrew word meaning “would that!.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַחֲלַי (H305) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 5:3, with occurrences in 2 Kings, Psalms.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַחֲלַי (H305) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַחֲלַי (H305) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַחֲלַי (ʼachălay) / H305 is traced through 2 Kings 5:3, Psalms 119:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H305. achalay אַחְלַי Psa 119:5 and אַחֲלֵי 2Kin 5:3 (perhaps from אָח III. and לַי = Aramaic לְוַי = ׃לוּ the varying punctuation is due doubtless to the word being treated by the punctuators as a substantive = wish , with suffix & in construct stative, 'my wish is that,' etc.; compare Ki on Psalm 119 וּבַקָּשׁוֺתַי תְּחִנּוֺתַי ), ah that! ( ᵐ5 ο[φελον ).
definitions.rootNote: or אַחֲלֵי ; prob from 253 and a variation of 3863 ;

occurrences.englishText: She said to her mistress, “I wish that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.”
Oh that my ways were steadfast
